cards.explanation: The answer is True. John says many of the Jews who had come to Mary, and had seen what Jesus did, believed in Him (John 11:45). They didn't just watch a dead man walk out of the tomb and shrug (John 11:44). Believing is where this whole passage starts, friends, and it's the part I like best.

The answer is that He's performing many signs. The council says, “This man is performing many signs.” (John 11:47) Notice what they don't say, friends. They don't argue that the signs didn't happen. I think that has them worried.

The answer is the Romans. The council says, “…everyone will believe in Him, and then the Romans will come and take away both our place and our nation.” (John 11:48) That's what they say they're afraid of, friends. The Romans were the empire that ruled the land back then (Luke 3:1).

The word is die. Caiaphas says, “…it is better for you that one man die for the people than that the whole nation perish.” (John 11:50) He's the high priest that year, and that's what he tells the room, friends. John explains right after that there's more going on in those words than Caiaphas said himself.

The answer is that He gathers them together into one. John says Jesus would die “…to gather them together into one.” (John 11:52) Scattered children, brought together, friends. I came out of a junk drawer, so a gathering like that gets me right in the apron.

The word is kill. John says, “So from that day on they plotted to kill Him.” (John 11:53) It's a heavy verse, friends, and I think it's okay to just say so. The plotting starts the very day Caiaphas speaks.

The town is Ephraim. Jesus withdrew “…to a town called Ephraim in an area near the wilderness. And He stayed there with the disciples.” (John 11:54) John says that's the result of the plot, friends, so Jesus stepped out of public view.

The answer is False. The crowds in the temple courts were asking each other, “What do you think? Will He come to the feast at all?” (John 11:56) That's a question, not a promise, friends. They kept looking for Him, and I think they couldn't say for sure what He'd do.

The orders are that anyone who knows where He is must report it. John says the chief priests and Pharisees “…had given orders that anyone who knew where He was must report it, so that they could arrest Him.” (John 11:57) The plot from verse 53 is turning into actual orders, friends. It's a heavy end to the passage.
